name: Weyerhaeuser
description: Weyerhaeuser is one of the world's largest private owners of timberland: it owns 9.7 million acres in the US (managing more than 10 million) and holds long-term licenses on 14 million acres in Canada. It grows and harvests trees and sells the logs, sells land that is worth more for development or other uses, collects rents and royalties from minerals, wind and solar, and runs 33 mills that make lumber, oriented strand board and engineered wood sold to home builders and dealers. It is a REIT, so timber income is largely untaxed at the corporate level and passes to shareholders. Wood products bring most of the sales but are swingy, and 2025 saw Wood Products Adjusted EBITDA fall to $250 million from $661 million on lower prices.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC 6798 (REIT). Weyerhaeuser qualifies as a REIT, but 72% of 2025 net sales come from manufacturing and distributing lumber, oriented strand board and engineered wood; the timber and land parts give most of the stable profit.

businessLines.name: Timberlands
businessLines.how: Sells logs, measured in thousand board feet in the West and green tons in the South, at market prices, both to its own Wood Products mills ($592M of intersegment sales in 2025) and to outside customers; revenue is log price times volume harvested, and Weyerhaeuser decides how much to harvest.
businessLines.description: Owns 9.7M US acres (managed more than 10M): 2.5M in Oregon and Washington and 6.7M in the South; long-term licenses on more than 14M acres in Canada. Sells logs to its own mills and to third parties.

revenue.note: net sales to unaffiliated customers, computed as total less the other two segments; 10-K says $1.5B. Segment net sales incl. intersegment $2,086M

businessLines.revenueNote: net sales to unaffiliated customers, computed as total less the other two segments; 10-K says $1.5B. Segment net sales incl. intersegment $2,086M

operatingProfit.note: net contribution to earnings, including gains on timberland sales

businessLines.name: Real Estate, Energy and Natural Resources (renamed Strategic Land Solutions from Q1 2026)
businessLines.how: Real Estate sells parcels at a price per acre (the 2025 increase was driven by a higher average price per acre sold); minerals and energy earn rents and royalties from operators who explore and produce on Weyerhaeuser land, with no capital spend by Weyerhaeuser; Climate Solutions sells services from land use for carbon and renewables. Sales are lumpy by year.
businessLines.description: Real Estate (sells timberland with higher value in other uses), Energy and Natural Resources (construction materials, industrial minerals, wind and solar, natural gas, easements, retained mineral interests) and Climate Solutions (launched 2021).

businessLines.name: Wood Products
businessLines.how: Buys logs (much from its own Timberlands) and sells finished lumber, OSB and engineered wood to dealers, do-it-yourself retailers, builders and industrial users at commodity market prices; profit is the price minus log and mill cost, so it swings with housing demand and lumber prices. 2025 net sales fell $264M on lower prices.
businessLines.description: Structural lumber, oriented strand board (OSB), engineered wood products and other specialty products from 33 manufacturing facilities in the US and Canada.

geography.method: Regional revenue tagged in the filing's own XBRL instance: full-year contexts with one geographic dimension (or segments named after places), alone or crossed only with operating segments or a revenue line of the income statement; regions must add up to the revenue line within 1 percent; a member equal to the sum of others is a subtotal; the main split is the largest set of members adding up to the total; anything not broken out is a computed remainder.
